step1_analysis.description: A sub-circuit of a semidynamic sparse-tree adder core, likely representing a dynamic evaluate/precharge stage. It features a precharge path (XM5, XM4, XM2) and an evaluate path (XM1, XM6, XM3).

paper_reference.title: A 4-GHz 130-nm Address Generation Unit With 32-bit Sparse-Tree Adder Core

t_fall_delay.description: Propagation delay from the evaluate input rising to the output falling.

sky130_expected.calculation: R_nmos ≈ 1 / (270µA/V² * (5µm/0.5µm) * (1.8V - 0.42V)) ≈ 270 Ω. Assuming a 10fF load, τ = R*C ≈ 2.7 ps. Delay is typically a few time constants.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports 152 ps for the full 32-bit adder core. A single stage in 130nm (or SKY130) with W=5µm and L=0.5µm will be much faster, around 20-50 ps depending on the load.

t_rise_delay.description: Propagation delay from the precharge input falling to the output rising.

sky130_expected.reasoning: PMOS mobility is lower, so the precharge rise time will be slower than the evaluate fall time.

avg_power.description: Average power consumption during active switching at 4 GHz.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on standard dynamic power equation for a single gate switching at the paper's target frequency of 4 GHz.

leakage_power.description: Static power consumption when inputs are held constant.

sky130_expected.calculation: P_leak = 1% of P_dyn ≈ 0.01 * 130µW = 1.3 µW. Actual SKY130 leakage for L=0.5µm devices is typically much lower (sub-nW).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper notes a 1% leakage component for the whole core. For a single gate with L=0.5µm (non-minimum length), leakage will be extremely small in SKY130.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure rise/fall propagation delays, average dynamic power, and static leakage power of the semidynamic ALU sub-circuit.
step3_testbench.spice:
* ALU sub-circuit testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

XM1 N1 LABEL_NET_0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N0 LABEL_NET_2 LABEL_NET_1 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 LABEL_NET_3 LABEL_NET_4 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N0 GND LABEL_NET_5 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N1 LABEL_NET_6 N0 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N1 GND LABEL_NET_3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

* Supplies
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VLABEL_NET_1 LABEL_NET_1 0 1.8
VLABEL_NET_5 LABEL_NET_5 0 1.8

* Inputs (Evaluate and Precharge)
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 PULSE(0 1.8 1n 50p 50p 1n 4n)
VLABEL_NET_6 LABEL_NET_6 0 PULSE(1.8 0 3n 50p 50p 1n 4n)
VLABEL_NET_2 LABEL_NET_2 0 1.8
VLABEL_NET_4 LABEL_NET_4 0 1.8

* Load capacitance
Cload N1 0 10f

.control
* Transient Analysis
tran 10p 8n

* Measure Delays
meas tran t_fall_delay trig v(LABEL_NET_0) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(N1) val=0.9 fall=1
meas tran t_rise_delay trig v(LABEL_NET_6) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(N1) val=0.9 rise=1

* Measure Average Power
let power = (-i(VVDD) - i(VLABEL_NET_1) - i(VLABEL_NET_5)) * 1.8
meas tran avg_power avg power from=0 to=8n

* DC Operating Point for Leakage
op
let leak_power = (-i(VVDD) - i(VLABEL_NET_1) - i(VLABEL_NET_5)) * 1.8
print leak_power

quit
.endc
